title: OBJ Sequence Export
content: **Objective** Export an OBJ Sequence as an OBJ file on every frame of an animation. Exporting a 1 second animation with a 30 fps standard will result in 30 OBJ files being exported. **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Animation ▶ **OBJ Sequence** **Operation** 1. 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Animation ▶ **OBJ Sequence** → The Save File window opens. 2. Select the desired file and click **OK**. → The Export OBJ Animation window opens. Set below options as needed and click **OK**. **Export OBJ Animation Option** **Object** | * **Select All Patterns:** Select/Deselect all patterns. You can select specific patterns by utilizing the dropdown menu on the right (ver2.2.0). ※ When utilizing the OBJ (Selected) menu, patterns selected in the 3D and 2D windows are automatically selected and checkbox-ed. * **Select All Avatars:** Select/Deselect all Avatars/Objects. You can select specific objects by utilizing the dropdown menu on the right (ver2.2.0). * **Select All Graphics and Trims:** Select/Deselect all Graphics and Trims. You can select specific stitches by utilizing the dropdown menu on the right (ver2.2.0). ---|--- **Single Object** Exports the selected object as a single object. ![Single Object.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53147275456409) | **Multiple Objects** Exports the selected object as multiple objects. ![Multiple Objects.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53147287895065) **UnWeld** Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. ※ Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version 2.3.0. (ver2.3.0). ![UnWeld.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53147275467929) | ******Weld** **** Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern **** that are sewn together into one line into one point. **** ![Weld.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53147287901209) **** * **Weld Selected Pattern:** Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns (ver2.3.0). **Thin** Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. ![Thin.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53147287903129) | **Thick** Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. ****![Thick.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53147275475865) * **Combined UV Coordinates** * **Include Internal Shape:** Include internal line and/or shape information in export (ver2.3.0). **Scale** | Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from “Unit in file to import” is selected. **Axis Conversion** | Changes the directions of each axis of the object. **Animation** | Entire Area (saves all of the recorded garment animation.) | Play Area Only (saves only the play area garment animation.) ****
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for exporting an OBJ sequence as individual OBJ files for each frame of an animation, enabling users to customize their export settings effectively.

title: [3D Tool] Edit Tack
content: **List of Contents** Edit Tack Delete Tack ### **Objective** Edit the position and the spacing of tacks/Avatar or delete unnecessary tacks. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ **Edit Tack** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit Tack.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53147028971545)**Edit Tack** **Operation** **Edit Tack** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ **Edit Tack** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit Tack.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53147028971545)**Edit Tack** → The Garment is now being changed to semi-transparent. 2. Click ▶ drag on the end point to adjust the position and spacing. **Delete Tack** 1. Click on a tack to delete. → The selected tack is now being highlighted in yellow color. 2. Press 'Delete' on keyboard, or right-click and select **Delete** among the pop-up menu option. → The selected tack is now being deleted. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for editing the position and spacing of tacks or deleting unnecessary tacks in your sewing project.

title: [Tool] Move Buttonhole
content: ### Objective Move buttonholes as desired. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Select/Move Button** 3D Window Toolbar ▶ [![Select_Move Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53147009912985)](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000887488) **Select/Move Button** **Operation** **Move Buttonholes with Click-and-Drag** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Select/Move Button** 3D Window Toolbar ▶ [![Select_Move Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53147009912985) ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000887488)**Select/Move Button** 2. Click and drag the buttonholes to the desired location on either of 2D or 3D Pattern. → The selected buttonholes are now being moved accordingly. **※ Note:** Move multiple buttonholes at once by selecting them in the 2D window (ver2.4.0). **Move Buttonholes with Distance Input (ver2.5.0)** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Select/Move Button** 3D Window Toolbar ▶ [![Select_Move Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53147009912985) ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000887488)**Select/Move Button** 2. While click-and-dragging the buttonholes with left-click mouse button, click right-click mouse button in either of 2D or 3D window. →The Moving Distance window appears. 3. Enter desired value in the menu. **Distance Moved** | Sets the moved distance of the buttonhole from its original location. ---|--- **Position** | Sets the position of the center of the buttonhole from the left/right/top/bottom of the pattern outline. 4. Click **OK**. → The buttonholes are now being moved according to the input value. **※ Note:****** Buttonholes can only be moved within the boundaries of the Pattern.
content_description: Learn how to easily select and reposition buttonholes in your design using click-and-drag or precise distance input methods.

title: [Popup] Mirror Paste Buttonhole
content: ### Objective Copy and mirror paste buttonholes (ver2.5.0). ### **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ **Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R)** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Select_Move Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146971468057) **Select/Move Button** ▶ Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ **Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R)** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ **Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R)** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Select_Move Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146971468057) **Select/Move Button** ▶ Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ **Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R)** 2. Click **Copy (Ctrl+C)** from the pop-up menu. 3. Right click on the copied buttonhole then click **Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R)** from the pop-up menu. → Placement preview displays along the mouse in the 2D window. 4. Click on a desired location to paste the buttonholes. **※ Note:** * Before pasting buttonholes in place, right click to access the Paste window where specific interval and number of buttonholes can be manually input for multiple copy-and-paste. * When buttonholes are mirror-pasted, only locations are mirrored whereas other properties, such as **Angle** , are not.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for users to efficiently copy and mirror paste buttonholes in CLO 3D, enhancing their design workflow.

title: Shrink Pattern
content: ### **Objective** Shrink or stretch 3D Garment Pattern horizontally and vertically without changing it in the 2D Pattern window. The default value is 100 percent (%) which indicates the natural state of the Garment material, in other words there is no artificial shrinkage or stretchiness. Use the function to express shrinkage after textile treatments such as garment washing, or use it temporarily to draw the inner layer against the avatar when dressing multiple layers of Garments for easier Simulation. **Location** Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Shrinkage Weft** /**Warp** **Operation** 1. Select a Pattern to shrink with 2D toolbar's ![Edit Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146812707353) **Edit Pattern** or ![Transform Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146825571737) **Transform Pattern**. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Shrinkage Weft** /**Warp** 3. Enter desired shrink values. → The Pattern in the 3D window is now being shrunk accordingly.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the horizontal and vertical dimensions of 3D garment patterns in simulation without altering their 2D representations, allowing for realistic textile treatment effects and layered garment fitting.

title: [Property] Create 2D Button Measurement
content: ### Objective View button position from the Pattern outline with 2D measurements (ver2.5.0). **Location** Object Browser ▶ Button Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ **To Center** **Operation** 1. Select a button with ![Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146788160921) **Select/Move Button** tool in the 3D toolbar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ **To Center** 3. Select the desired 2D measurement options of the **left** /**right** /**up** /**down**. → The 2D measurement is now being displayed or hidden accordingly.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on how to view and adjust the position of a button using 2D measurements in the Pattern Outline (ver2.5.0).

title: Copy Buttonhole Style
content: ### **Objective** Copy and modify a buttonhole in order to create a new buttonhole style or adjust its properties. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ ![Copy.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146771919897) **Copy** **Operation** 1. Navigate to the Object Browser and select an item in the buttonhole tab. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ ![Copy.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146771919897) **Copy** → A new buttonhole item with the same properties of the selected item is now being created.
content_description: Learn how to copy and modify buttonholes to create custom styles or adjust existing properties in the Object Browser's Buttonhole Tab.

title: [Object Browser] Copy Topstitch Style
content: **Objective** Copy and modify an existing Topstitch style in order to change its properties. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ ![Copy.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146767283609) **Copy** **Operation** 1. Object Browser ▶ Select a Topstitch style to copy 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ ![Copy.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146767283609) **Copy** → A new Topstitch style with the same properties of the selected Topstitch style is now being copied.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for copying and modifying an existing Topstitch style within the Object Browser to customize its properties.

title: [Object Browser] Delete Topstitch Style
content: ### Objective Delete unnecessary Topstitch styles. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Topstitch Style ▶ ![Delete.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146670569241) **Delete** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Topstitch Style ▶ ![Delete.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146670569241) **Delete** → The selected Topstitch style is now being deleted. **※ Note:** * It is also possible to delete by pressing the Delete key on the keyboard. * A Topstitch style can only be deleted when it is not applied on a Topstitch by clicking the ![Delete.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146670569241) **Delete** button.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for deleting unnecessary Topstitch styles in the Object Browser.

title: Create/Delete Reference Line
content: ### **List of Contents** Create Delete ### **Objective** Create Reference Line as needed to check its original shape when editing the Pattern. ### **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ **![Transform Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146407540505)Transform Pattern** ### **Operation** **Create** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. 2. Right-click on the pattern for which you want to create a reference line, and then click the **Clone as Reference Line** menu. 3. Modify the pattern. → You can check the shape of the original pattern as a reference line. **Delete** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. 2. Right-click on the pattern where you want to delete the reference line, and then click the **Delete Reference Line** menu. → The created Reference Line is deleted. **※Note:** Select Reference line with [Trace](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307728-Trace) tool to trace as internal line/shape. (ver 7.2 [![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/26243706096281)](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=YmCaqCFahmGfV1sM&t=1843)) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a guide for creating and deleting reference lines in the Transform Pattern tool, enabling users to maintain the original shape of their patterns during editing.

title: Adjust Avatar Location
content: ### **Objective** Adjust avatar location by using its X-Ray joint points. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Avatar ▶ **Show X-Ray Joints (Shift + X)** 3D Window ▶ ![Avatar Display.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146382280217) Avatar Display (Mouse-over) ▶![Show X-ray Joints.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146369394841)**Show X-Ray Joints (Shift + X)** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Avatar ▶ **Show X-Ray Joints (Shift + X)** 3D Window ▶ ![Avatar Display.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146382280217) Avatar Display (Mouse-over) ▶![Show X-ray Joints.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146369394841)**Show X-Ray Joints (Shift + X)** 2. Select purple point (pelvis point) in the middle of the avatar. 3. Click and drag or move it with the Gizmo to relocate the avatar.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on adjusting avatar positions using X-Ray joint points in a 3D environment.

title: [Style Property] Buttonhole Name
content: ### Objective Rename buttonholes as desired. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ **Change Name** ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ **Change Name** 2. Type in the desired name. → The name is now being edited and applied.
content_description: "Learn how to easily rename buttonholes in the Object Browser using the Property Editor."

title: Solidify
content: ### **Objective** Maintain desired draping state per pattern unit. For instance, solidify creases on the back of the knee area of a pair of jeans to maintain its shape while simulating (ver2.5.0). **Location** 3D Garment Right-click Pop-up Menu ▶**Solidify** **Operation** 1. 3D Toolbar ▶Select a 3D Pattern with ![Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146205100057) **Select/Move** tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Garment Right-click Pop-up Menu ▶ **Solidify** → The selected Pattern is now being solidified. 3. Follow the indicated guideline and adjust the **Strength** : Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Bond/Skive ▶ Solidify ▶ **Strength** → The selected Pattern's 3D shape is now being solidified according to the **Strength** value. **※ Note:** The higher the **Strength** value, the better the sustenance.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide on solidifying the draping state of pattern units in 3D garment design to enhance shape retention, particularly in areas like the back of the knee on jeans.

title: Delete Avatar Tape
content: ### **Objective** Delete avatar tapes. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ **Edit Measure (Avatar)** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit Measure.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146061175449) **Edit Measure (Avatar)** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ **Edit Measure (Avatar)** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit Measure.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146061175449) **Edit Measure (Avatar)** 2. Click on a tape to delete. → The tape is highlighted in yellow. 3. Press Delete key on keyboard. → The selected tape is now being deleted.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for deleting avatar tapes in the editing interface of a 3D design tool.

title: Fold Arrangement
content: ### **Objective** Fold Seam Allowances, collars and cuffs before activating the **Simulation** for better stability. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 3D ▶ **Fold** ▶ **Fold Arrangement** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Fold Arrangement.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53145879346713)**Fold Arrangement** **Operation** 1. After arranging Patterns, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D ▶ **Fold** ▶ **Fold Arrangement** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Fold Arrangement.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53145879346713)**Fold Arrangement** → The entire Internal Line/Shape of a 3D Garment appears. 2. Click on an Internal Line/Shape to fold. → The folding **Gizmo** appears. 3. Rotate the red or green axis along the blue circle as desired. → The selected pattern area is folded accordingly. → If the pattern is symmetrical, it is folded symmetrically. (ver 6.1) **※ Note:** Folding Internal Line/Shape is also available after simulating/draping the Garment.
content_description: Learn how to effectively fold seam allowances, collars, and cuffs in your 3D garment design for enhanced stability before initiating the simulation.

title: Spiral Pattern (ver 6.1)
content: ### **Objective** Create a Spiral pattern in a 2D window. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V4HDEKiJ0Og **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Create ▶ **Spiral** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Spiral.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53145732062105) **Spiral** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click the 2D window. → The Create Spiral Window appears. 3. After setting the options below, click OK. **Radius** | Set the radius at which a spiral pattern rotates. ---|--- **Length** | Set the length of the inner/outer segment of the spiral pattern. **Side** | Set the inside/outside width of the spiral pattern. **Offset** | Adjust the spacing between spirals. The length you enter is the distance from the center of the spiral pattern to the center of the next spiral layer. **Direction** | Set the rotation direction (clockwise/counterclockwise) of the spiral pattern. → A spiral pattern is created.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating a customizable spiral pattern in a 2D window, complete with options for radius, length, side, offset, and direction.

title: Hi/Low-Resolution Garment
content: ### **Objective** Enhance or lower the resolution of Garments. Use this function to enhance the Garment completion in order to emphasize reality and higher quality of a Garment and on the other hand, reduce it for faster adjustments. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 3D ▶**Hi-Res Garment** / **Low-Res Garment** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Hi_Res Garment.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144481358233) **Hi-Res Garment** / ![Low_Res Garment.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144481367833) **Low-Res Garment** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D ▶**Hi-Res Garment** / **Low-Res Garment** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Hi_Res Garment.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144481358233) **Hi-Res Garment** / ![Low_Res Garment.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144481367833) **Low-Res Garment** → Hi/Low-Res Properties window appears. 2. Adjust the value for each item. **Garment** | **Particle Distance** | Sets the Particle Distance value applying to all Patterns. \- Hi-Res Garment default value: 5mm \- Low-Res Garment default value: 20mm ---|---|--- **Tolerance** | Applies only for Patterns within the range of application of Particle Distance. The default tolerance value is between 5mm ~ 20mm, and any Pattern within the range set above is going to be applied. **※ Note:** This is provided to maintain the particle distance value of small patterns below 5mm for more stable simulation. Being mindful of the tolerance can avoid unintentional changes to these patterns. **Add'l Thickness - Collision** | Sets the collision thickness value applying to all patterns. \- Hi-Res Garment default value: 1mm \- Low-Res Garment default value: 2.5mm **Tolerance** | Any Pattern within the range set above is going to be applied. **Avatar** | **Skin Offset** | Sets the skin offset value applying to avatar. \- Hi-Res Garment default value: 0mm \- Low-Res Garment default value: 3mm **Tolerance** | Any Avatar within the range set above is going to be applied. **Simulation** | **Simulation Quality** | Sets the simulation quality as **Complete** or **Normal**. \- Hi-Res Garment default value: **Complete** \- Low-Res Garment default value: **Normal** **※ Note:** Set the simulation quality on **Complete** for material properties generated in Emulator Mode to result the most accurate simulation. However it may slow down the simulation speed therefore it is recommended to apply this setting when enhancing the garment completion. **Check On/Off Menus** | Toggle option whether to apply on Garment, Avatar, Simulation settings. 3. Click **OK** button. → The adjustments are now being applied. 4. Activate the Simulation. → The adjustments are now being applied to Garment Simulation.
content_description: This web page provides guidance for enhancing or lowering the resolution of garments in order to improve visual quality or facilitate faster adjustments during the design process.

title: Add Perpendicular Internal Line
content: **List of Contents** Add from a Point Add from a Segment **Objective** Create Internal Lines perpendicular to Pattern outlines or 2D window. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144373593625) **Edit Pattern** **Operation** **Add from a Point** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144373593625) **Edit Pattern** 2. Right click on the point of a Pattern outline or Internal Line. →The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Hover the mouse over the **Add Perpendicular Internal Line** option. → Below options appear. **X-Axis** | Can type in Internal Line's angle based on 2D window's X-axis. ---|--- **Y-Axis** | Can type in Internal Line's angle based on 2D window's Y-axis. **Local** | Can type in Internal Line's angle based on the selected segment. 4. Select the desired option. →The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window with different options appears based on your selection. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- | X-Axis/ Y-Axis | Local (Pattern outline) | Local (Internal Line) Angle | Type in the angle for the Internal Line. As the default angle is 90º, you may easily create Internal Line perpendicularly. Length | Type in Internal Line's length. Extend | When the option is toggled on, the Internal Line extends to Pattern outlines. When the **Length** value is different from the length when it is extended, the option turns off automatically. Both (ver5.0.0) | Add Internal Line on both sides of the selected point. Opposite Segment | Not Applicable | Internal Line is created based on the other side of the selected line. Reverse | Not Applicable | The Internal Line is reversed. **Add from a Segment** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144373593625) **Edit Pattern** 2. Right click on the Pattern outline or Internal Line. →The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select **Add Perpendicular Internal Line**. → The Internal Line preview appears at the center of the selected Pattern outline or Internal Line. → The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window appears. 4. Configure below options as needed and click OK. Option | Description ---|--- Angle | Type in the angle for the Internal Line. As the default angle is 90º, you may easily create Internal Line perpendicularly. Length | Type in the length of the Internal Line. Distance to Segment Edge | Locate the Internal Line. The Internal Line preview shifts as number changes. Extend | When the option is toggled on, the Internal Line extends to Pattern outlines. When the **Length** value is different from the length when it is extended, the option turns off automatically. Both (ver5.0.0) | Add Internal Line on both sides of the selected line. Reverse | The Internal Line is reversed. → The Internal Line is created accordingly. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on how to add perpendicular internal lines to patterns in a 2D editing environment, detailing step-by-step instructions and options for customization.

title: 2D Snapshot (1:1)
content: **Objective** Save real size 2D pattern (1:1). **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Snapshot ▶ **2D Pattern (1:1)** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Snapshot ▶ **2D Pattern (1:1)** → 2D window is enlarged, 2D Snapshot window appears. 2. Set below details as needed. 3. Locate the patterns according to the selected setting size (paper), Click **Save**. **Size** | **Preset** | Customize or select from provided preset options. ---|---|--- **Orientation** | Select from portrait or landscape orientation options. **Resolution** | Sets the pixels per inch for the image. **Options** | **Fabric Image** | View or hide the fabric image. **Graphic Image** | View or hide the graphic image. **Reset** | Resets the options back to the program default settings. 4. In order to save the file, enter desired file name and location, then click **Save**. → The image can be saved in .png or .pdf file format. **※ Note:** * Now you can select segments with the ![Edit Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144211277081) **Edit Pattern** tool and the selected segments will be highlighted in the 2D Snapshot image (ver3.2.0). * Prior to saving the 2D Snapshot image, you can now arrange patterns with the ![Transform Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144275855641) **Transform Pattern** tool (ver3.2.0). * Save the image background as transparent (ver3.2.0). * Toggle symmetry, instance, trims, and measurements for graphics on or off (ver3.2.0). * 2D snapshots can only be saved as .png format in ver4.0.0 and below.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for saving a 2D pattern as a 1:1 snapshot, including customization options for size, orientation, and resolution.

title: Align
content: **Objective** Align Patterns and Internal Shapes based on various standards (ver2.5.0). **Location** Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/ Internal Shape) ▶ Align ▶ **Left** / **Center** / **Right** / **Top** / **Middle** / **Bottom** **Operation** 1. Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![Transform Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144247934361) **Transform Pattern** tool. 2. Select two or more Patterns or/and Internal Shapes. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/ Internal Shape) ▶ Align ▶ **Left** / **Center** / **Right** / **Top** / **Middle** / **Bottom** →The Patterns or/and Internal Shapes align to the Pattern or Internal Shape that is right clicked on. **※Note:** You can also align Pattern outlines or Internal Lines using the ![2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115001011167) **Edit Pattern** tool. However, be mindful that the aligning segments may transform their Patterns or Internal Shapes.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for aligning patterns and internal shapes using the right-click pop-up menu in version 2.5.0.

title: Create Custom Blocks
content: **List of Contents** Open Modular Template Load and Place Patterns Sew Patterns and Block Boxes ## **Objective** Create a Block of a desired Garment and apply it to your design. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Click the Mode button on the right top corner ▶ **MODULAR** ## **Operation** **Open Modular Template** 1. Click the **Modular Template Presets** on the right top corner of Block Editor. → Modular Template Presets window appears. 2. Select a desired Garment category and Modular Template type, click **OK**. → The selected Modular Template appears in the 2D window. **Load and Place Patterns** 1. Add desired Garment files to place into the Block Boxes. 2. Place the Patterns of added Garment to the Blcok Boxes. → The Patterns are linked into the Block Boxes. → The Patterns are automatically arranged to the avatar in 3D Window. (ver 7.0) 3. Sew Patterns to Blcok Boxes, then Simulate. **Sew Patterns and Block Boxes** 1. Click on **![Segment Sewing.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144062952089)Segment Sewing** or ![Free Sewing.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144082386073) **Free Sewing** tool. 2. Sew Patterns and Block Boxes. **※ Note:** * Patterns that are sewn alone ( i.e. hems, sleeves or armholes of a sleeveless style) do not need to be sewn to Block Boxes. * When sewing Block Boxes and Blocks, M:N Sewing cannot be used. Only 1:N Sewing can be used for Block Boxes to be 1. * Difference in length between the actual Patterns and the Block Boxes has no effect on the Simulation. * To show Sewing Lines between Block Boxes and Patterns, activate the ![Show Modular Sewing_Show.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144062963353)**Show Modular Sewing/Show Pattern Sewing** tool. This tool is activated by default in the Modular Mode. Click it again to either hide or show all Sewing Lines. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for creating and customizing garment blocks using modular templates and sewing patterns in the Block Editor.

title: Attach to Measure
content: ### **Objective** Attach avatar tapes to internal or external seam/pattern lines. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ **Attach to Measure** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Attach to Avatar Tape.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53143897923097) **Attach to Avatar Tape** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ **Attach to Measure** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Attach to Avatar Tape.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53143897923097) **Attach to Measure** 2. In the 3D window, select seam or pattern line to attach to avatar tape. → Pattern with the selected line becomes transparent and the selected line gets highlighted in red. 3. Select avatar tape to be attached. → Once it is selected, the pattern becomes normal, the attached seam or pattern line and the avatar tape becomes in red. 4. To detach avatar tape from seam or pattern line, click on **Attach to Avatar Tape** tool again, and press 'Delete' on keyboard.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for attaching and detaching avatar tapes to seam or pattern lines within the CLO 3D software.

title: Internal Polygon/Line
content: ### **Objective** Create Internal Polygons and Lines inside a Pattern. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Polygon/Line** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Internal Polygon_Line.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53143609271321) **Internal Polygon/Line** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Polygon/Line** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Internal Polygon_Line.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53143609271321) **Internal Polygon/Line** 2. Click within a Pattern to establish the start point of an Internal Polygon/Line. 3. Drag the mouse and click as needed to freehand the Internal Polygon/Line. 4. Right click while freehanding the Internal Polygon/Line to access the Create Internal Polygon/Line window. 5. Use**Length** , **Mirror Creation,** and **Position** options to create the Internal Polygon/Line more precisely and conveniently. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Length** | Length | Designate the length to be created next. When the **Mirror Creation** option is active, the Length will be applied to the mirrored line as well. **Option** **(ver5.0.0)** | Mirror Creating | The Internal Polygon/Line is created symmetrically. The starting point converts to a closed point. Axis | Local | Symmetric lines are created based on the starting point (local). X-Axis | Symmetric lines are created based on the X-Axis. Y-Axis | Symmetric lines are created based on the Y-Axis. **Position** | Left | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its left. Right | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its right. Top | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its top. Bottom | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its bottom. 6. To complete an Internal Polygon, click the start point. On the other hand, to complete an Internal Line, double click the last point. **※ Note:****** * Right click inside a Pattern to open the Create Internal Polygon window and type in desired values. → An Internal Polygon is created with the designated values (ver2.5.0). * Click inside a Pattern to create the start point of an Internal Line. Then, drag and right click to open the Create Internal Polygon window. Enter desired values. → An Internal Line is created with the designated values (ver2.5.0). * Hold down the Ctrl key as creating an Internal Polygon/Line to create curves. * Hold down the Shift key to drag the mouse in straight lines or in 45º diagonal lines.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating internal polygons and lines within a pattern using the 2D Toolbar in the software.

title: Ellipse
content: **List of Contents** Create Create with Specific Values **Objective** Create ellipse or circle Patterns in the 2D window. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Create ▶ **Ellipse** 2D Toolbar ▶ **![Ellipse.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53143417395737)Ellipse** **Operation** **Create** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Create ▶ **Ellipse** 2D Toolbar ▶ **![Ellipse.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53143417395737)Ellipse** 2. Click and drag on the 2D window. → A preview of an ellipse appears. **※ Note:** * Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a circle. * While creating the Pattern, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to create it by the center point (ver.5.1.0). * While creating the Pattern, press down the Shift + Ctrl keys to create a full circle by its center point (ver.5.1.0). 3. Release the mouse when the desired shape is achieved. → The ellipse Pattern is created. **Create with Specific Values** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Create ▶ **Ellipse** 2D Toolbar ▶ **![Ellipse.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53143417395737)****Ellipse** 2. Click in the 2D window. → The Create Ellipse window appears. 3. Type in the desired values for the options below. **Diameter** | Set the diameter of the circle Pattern. ---|--- **Radius** | Set the radius of the circle Pattern (ver3.2.0). **![img_ratio_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115008599147)**| Link to maintain the width and height ratio. **Circumference** | Set the circumference of the circle Pattern (ver3.2.0). Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for creating ellipse and circle patterns in a 2D window using specific values and keyboard shortcuts.

title: Add/Apply Grading
content: #### **List of Contents** Add Grading Apply Grading Grading Properties #### **Add and Apply patterns of multiple sizes.** **** #### #### **Add Grading** 1. Click the ![add text.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37933934400153) button in the **Grading tab** ![Grading tab.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53143083105561) in the Object Browser. 2. Click the ![add.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39591836604057) **Add Size** button next to Size Group to add a new size to the group. **📝 Note:** Open the RUL file corresponding to the pattern by clicking ![open.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37933934416025) **Open Grade Rule** on the right side of the Size Group. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37933919226905) ### ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39591932902937) In Size Groups, you can add/insert smaller sizes or sizes in between at any point. 1. Right-click on a size in a size group, and then click the **Insert 1 Size Above** menu. ![Trim Grading.gif](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37933934428953) 2. For adding bigger sizes, click the ![add.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39591836604057) **Add Size** button next to Size Group. #### #### **Apply Grading** 1. Click the 2D pattern using the ![Transform Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37933919244057)**Transform Pattern** or ![Edit Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37933934445593)**Edit Pattern** tool in the 2D toolbar. 2. Click ![Assign to Selected Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53143063656601) **Assign to Selected Pattern** button next to Size Group. 3. Or Click ![assign text.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37933934462233) button to assign to new grading rule. #### #### **Grading Properties** 1. Click the Size Group. 2. Set the following properties. **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Name** | Set the name of the Size Group and Size. **Show** | Shows or hides the grading segments displayed in the 2D pattern. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for adding and applying grading patterns of various sizes in the CLO 3D design software.

title: Select/Move Point/Segment
content: **List of Contents** Select Move ### **Objective** Modify Patterns, Internal, and Base (ver5.2) Shapes by moving points and segments. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115012650767/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png)**Edit Pattern** **Operation** **Select** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115012650767/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png)**Edit Pattern** 2. Click a point or segment of a Pattern or Internal Shape. → The point or segment is selected. → When there are multiple points or segments, a pop-up menu appears allowing you to select the desired one (ver3.0.0.) 3. To select multiple points and segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard when clicking them. → All clicked points and segments are selected. 4. Or, click and drag on the 2D window to encompass points and segments to be selected with the marquee box. → All points and segments inside the marquee box are selected. **Move** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000037147)**Transform Pattern** 2. Click and drag the Pattern or use the [arrow keys](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000376767-%EB%B0%A9%ED%96%A5%ED%82%A4%EB%A1%9C-%EC%9D%B4%EB%8F%99). 3. Hold down the Shift key or Ctrl key (Mac: command) while moving the point or segment. → The point or segment can be moved in precise vertical, horizontal, or diagonal lines, or in its slope.→ The center point of the dart is moved along the direction of the center line's tilt **(ver 7.3**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142637530649)**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=mOQg7GggSZkBW3dn&t=2557)**)** 4. Or, right click or hit F1 key (Mac: Ctrl) while moving the point or segment to type in distance moved. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Distance Moved** | Type in the how much a segment or a point is moved. **X-Axis (ver4.2.0)** | Type in how much a point is moved on x-axis. This option does not appear for segments. **Y-Axis (ver4.2.0)** | Type in how much a point is moved on Y-axis. This option does not appear for segments. **※ Note:** If it is cumbersome to select Patterns using the ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000037167) **Edit Pattern** tool, use the ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000037147) **Transform Pattern** tool. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for modifying patterns in the CLO 3D software by selecting and moving points and segments within the 2D pattern editor.

title: Clone as Pattern/Internal Shape
content: **List of Contents** Clone as Pattern Clone as Pattern (with Sewing) **Objective** Duplicate an Internal Shape as an identical shaped Pattern or vice-versa. **Operation** **Clone as Pattern** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ **Transform Pattern (A)** 2. Right click on the Internal Shape to be duplicated as a Pattern to access the pop-up menu. Then, select **Clone as Pattern**. →The duplicated Pattern follows along the mouse cursor. 3. Click on the 2D window to place the Pattern. **Clone as Pattern (with Sewing) (ver 7.3**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142583405721)**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=247F8mM4Cy2xRw62&t=2656)**)** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar **▶Edit Pattern (Z)** 2. Click the Pattern to be duplicated and the connecting segment to be automatically sewn. Then, right-click ▶ click the **Clone as Pattern (with Sewing)**. → It is duplicated in a pattern connecting the start/end points of the selected segment. → The duplicated pattern follows along the mouse cursor. 3. Click on the desired Pattern to place the Internal Shape. → It is duplicated with the selected internal line automatically sewn. **※ Note:** When the internal shape is selected and clone as a pattern (with Sewing), the entire pattern is sewn. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to duplicate internal shapes as patterns in Clo3D, both with and without sewing connections.

title: Puckering Properties and Options
content: **Objective** Edit Puckering properties individually. ### **Location** 2D Window Toolbar▶ ![Edit_Puckering.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026732287) Edit Puckering ### **Operation** 1. Select a segment of applied puckering using the tool in the Location. → Puckering properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Adjust the properties as needed. **Property** | **Description** ---|--- **Name** | Rename the Puckering. Puckering Property | Change the Puckering style applied to the selected segment. **Extend** | Extend the start/endpoint of the puckering to the 2D pattern outline. **Placement** | Select the desired placement by checking Both Sides. **Offset** | **Offset** | Adjust the distance between a puckering and a pattern outline. Include the Puckering Width in Offset or not if needed. **Z-Offset** | Adjust the distance between Z-axis and a pattern piece. 3. Or, Right-click on the puckering to apply the options as needed. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- **Select All with Same property** | Select the puckerings with the same properties as the selected puckering. Assign to New Puckering | Add and apply a new puckering style. **Delete** | Delete puckering. Remove Linked Editing (ver 7.3[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142579528985)**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=1MYK1oK7nBcI3_Hr&t=3110)) | Remove linked edtiting of the symmetric puckering.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for individually editing puckering properties within a 2D window toolbar, including selection, adjustment options, and menu functionalities.

title: Shape Dart Cap
content: ### **Objective** Smooth Pattern outlines with darts. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ ![edit_pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000764568) **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ **Edit Pattern** **Operation** 1. [Create a dart on a segment.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115008753767-%EC%99%B8%EA%B3%BD-%EB%8B%A4%ED%8A%B8) 2. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 3. Right-click on the dart and select **Shape Dart Cap**. → The Shape Dart Cap is displayed in light blue. 4. Click a curve point ▶ Drag to smooth the connected line. Or, Click where there is no curve point to add and edit the curve point. (**ver 7.3**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142522554521)**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=RvRZ3gIAX2lpvmnu&t=2492)) 5. Adjust curvature then press Enter. → Shape Dart Cap is completed and the center line is created as the baseline. **※Note:** If necessary, click the curve point to delete it with the Delete key. (ver 6.1)
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and editing smooth pattern outlines with darts in the CLO 3D software.

title: Ruler & Guidelines
content: **List of Contents** Show/Hide Ruler and Setting Create and Move Guideline Set Guideline Options ### **Objective** Place 2D elements or create pattern using Ruler and Guidelines in 2D Window. ### **** **Location** 2D Tool bar ▶ **Transform Pattern (A)** or **Edit Pattern (Z)** ### **Operation** **Show/Hide Ruler and Setting** 1. 2D Window ▶ ![2d_information.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/24377563125657) 2D Information ▶ Click ![ruler.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/24377563129113) **Show Ruler.** → Ruler appears in 2D window. 2. Right click on Ruler and change the unit(Inch, Centimeter, Millimeter). 3. Click and drag the cross point on the top left of the tape measure to change the origin point. **Create and Move Guideline** 1. Click the tool/ menu indicated. 2. Click either the vertical or the horizontal ruler ▶ Drag it → A guideline is created.. 3. Or right click on a segment to be a reference of a guideline or two points and click**Create a Guideline Along Points.** → A guideline is created based on the selected points or the segment. 4. Click the created guideline ▶ Drag it to move. While dragging, Right-click to enter the Moving distance directly. → the guide line is moved. **Set Guideline Options** 1. Click the tool/ menu indicated. 2. Right-click on the guideline and set options as needed. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- **Offset Guideline** **(ver 7.3**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142495517081)**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=MxI8TD8x9LxzbDjP&t=2449)**)** | Create a new guideline at[ regular intervals ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en/articles/115000346488-%EB%82%B4%EB%B6%80%EC%84%A0%EB%B6%84-%EC%83%9D%EC%84%B1#Click1)based on the selected guideline. **Lock Guideline** **(ver 7.3)** | Lock the selected guideline. 2D Window ▶ ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900007297086) 2D Pattern Lock ▶ Click ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900007297066) **Lock Guideline.** Click the icon so tha all guidelines are not selected. Right-Click on empty space on the 2Dwindow and select **Unlock All Guidelines** to unlock the guidelines. **Delete Guideline/** **Delete All Guidelines** | Delete the selected guideline or delete all guidelines. **※Note:** * Click Ruler ▶ Hit the Ctrl key on the keyboard when click-and-dragging the guideline or hold the Ctrl key and click the guideline to convert its direction. * Use ![Toolbar_2D_Shape_Trace.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360017978773) [Trace tool](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000307728-%ED%8A%B8%EB%A0%88%EC%9D%B4%EC%8A%A4) to trace as internal shape or pattern. When creating and moving a guideline, it snaps to segment points on a pattern. (ver 6.1) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions for utilizing the Ruler and Guidelines in the 2D Window to effectively place 2D elements and create patterns.
